evidence.estrutura: Clark governed within New Zealand’s unitary parliamentary system while working with local and international institutions; no strong structural extremity is evident.
evidence.representacao: Her long elected parliamentary career, opposition leadership and premiership strongly support representative democracy.
evidence.poder: She governed through rule-bound democratic institutions and accepted national-security agencies, supporting a liberal but not anti-state position.
evidence.imigracao: New Zealand Labour politics under Clark generally supported a diverse immigration society with regulation; this fits pluralist but managed migration.
evidence.diplomacia: Foreign-affairs, disarmament and UNDP leadership strongly support multilateral diplomacy and international institutions.
evidence.intervencao: Her internationalist record emphasizes multilateral legitimacy and development cooperation more than unilateral military force.
evidence.economia: Labour governments combined private markets with high public investment in health, education and welfare; social-democratic mixed economy.
evidence.controle: Public services, labor policy and social investment imply meaningful regulation without command planning.
evidence.comercio: New Zealand remained highly trade-oriented and internationally integrated; relatively open commerce with social regulation.
evidence.religiao: Her public politics are secular and institutional rather than religiously grounded.
evidence.moral: Labour social policy and inclusion place her on the socially progressive side, though within mainstream institutional politics.
evidence.tecnologia: Public administration and development work show pragmatic use of science and technology rather than ideological accelerationism.
